documents.abstract: This presentation examines media hate speech as an instrument of information warfare and a factor contributing to social destabilization, democratic erosion, and threats to national security, with particular attention to Russia's war against Ukraine. The presentation explores the role of hate speech in Russian information warfare, identifying three principal functions: the dehumanization of Ukrainians, the justification of military aggression, and the mobilization of public support for hostile policies. It examines how discriminatory narratives and hostile rhetoric circulate through traditional media, social networks, and digital communication platforms, including their international dissemination. Special attention is given to the manifestations of hate speech within Ukrainian society during wartime, including linguistic, religious, political, and social divisions. The presentation highlights the risks associated with polarization, the normalization of hostility, and the weakening of democratic culture. A substantial part of the analysis focuses on artificial intelligence and deepfake technologies as emerging instruments of information manipulation. Through international case studies, the presentation illustrates how synthetic media can impersonate political leaders, celebrities, journalists, and other public figures, facilitate disinformation campaigns, undermine public trust, and contribute to gender-based harassment. The presentation also examines regulatory responses, including the European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act, the Digital Services Act, and Denmark's proposed legal framework for protecting individuals against unauthorized digital imitations of their appearance and voice. The presentation concludes that effective responses to media hate and AI-enabled manipulation require an integrated approach combining legal safeguards, platform accountability, technological transparency, rapid intervention, media literacy, and public awareness. Particular emphasis is placed on protecting human dignity, democratic resilience, and fundamental rights in an increasingly AI-driven information environment.

documents.abstract: Integrasi Kecerdasan Buatan (Artificial Intelligence/AI) ke dalam berbagai ekosistem digitaldan infrastruktur web telah membawa transformasi efisiensi yang signifikan. Namun,akselerasi adopsi teknologi ini melahirkan kompleksitas baru di bidang etika digital, privasidata, dan ketahanan siber. Artikel independen ini menyajikan analisis mendalam mengenailanskap risiko tata kelola AI, mencakup eksplorasi data over-collection, ancaman modelinversion attacks, bias struktural algoritma, hingga masalah opakitas (black box). Selainmemetakan ancaman, tulisan ini merumuskan kerangka kerja operasional Responsible AI yangmemadukan prinsip Data Minimization, Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning (PPML),Explainable AI (XAI), serta penyelarasan regulasi nasional (UU No. 27 Tahun 2022 tentangPDP) dan internasional (EU AI Act).Kata Kunci: Kecerdasan Buatan, Etika Digital, Keamanan Data, Responsible AI, BiasAlgoritma, Explainable AI, Privacy-Preserving ML.

documents.abstract: Perkembangan Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) mulai mengubah cara mahasiswa belajar dan menghasilkan produk akademik dalam pendidikan keperawatan. Perubahan ini menimbulkan pertanyaan mengenai kompetensi yang perlu dibangun dan bukti pembelajaran yang perlu dihasilkan melalui asesmen. Kajian ini bertujuan meninjau kembali implikasi GenAI terhadap pendidikan keperawatan dengan mensintesis perubahan pembelajaran, asesmen, AI literacy, human judgment, serta kurikulum dan tata kelola. Kajian menggunakan integrative literature review dengan tahapan Whittemore dan Knafl. Penelusuran melalui Scopus untuk publikasi 2023–2026 menghasilkan 538 rekaman. Setelah pengelolaan duplikasi dan evaluasi literatur, 11 sumber ditetapkan sebagai core evidence dan 7 sebagai supporting literature. Analisis menghasilkan enam tema: perubahan cara belajar; efisiensi dan kedalaman belajar; redesain asesmen; AI literacy; human judgment; serta kurikulum dan tata kelola. Sintesis menunjukkan bahwa GenAI dapat memperluas interaksi dan efisiensi pembelajaran, tetapi tidak otomatis menghasilkan pembelajaran yang lebih mendalam. Karena itu, asesmen perlu semakin menampilkan reasoning, verifikasi, penerapan, komunikasi, dan performa. Integrasi GenAI dalam pendidikan keperawatan perlu diarahkan pada penguatan kompetensi profesional dan tanggung jawab manusia.

documents.abstract: With the global mental health care crisis (WHO, 2025), artificial intelligence (AI) tools are being explored as viable options for support. Their support for the mental health of students with gifts and talents (SWGT) is examined here. AI tools may be purpose-built for mental health support or companionship or designed for general assistance. The foundational large language model (LLM) for each of these is trained on different materials, which may not contain up-to-date information relevant to SWGT. SWGT should be educated on issues related to privacy and security, the possibility of false or misinformation from the AI tool, the prioritization of user engagement over helpful responding, and the dangers of overinvolvement. Talent development may be affected by the use of AI tools not trained to encourage psychosocial skills associated with success in the student’s domain of gifts or talents. Some controls are recommended to support SWGT’s positive use of AI.

documents.abstract: The work focuses on the development of a method for selecting diagnostic features in the milling of materials with significantly different properties. The use of two very different materials allowed for better generalization of the conclusions. The research concentrated on steel and composite materials, defined as combinations of two or more materials with diverse chemical and mechanical properties. A method for assessing the usefulness of measured physical quantities for predicting tool wear using machine learning techniques was proposed. Both vibration signals and cutting forces were considered, but the proposed method is general. The study implements artificial intelligence methods through the practical deployment of multiple machine‑learning models trained on vibration‑ and force‑based features. The methodology is based on a measure of the significance of data partitioning into subsets created from forces and vibration accelerations, combined with a large set of supervised machine learning methods, including classification and regression algorithms with various hyperparameters. This approach enables a relatively objective statistical assessment of the usefulness of a given physical quantity in monitoring tool condition.

The technology of Generative AI is now capable not only of writing, painting, and composing, but even transforming the work of others. While India's Copyright Act, 1957 was framed taking humans into consideration as the creators, yet there is an exception for Computer Generated Works and an additional set of Moral Rights provided for in Section 57. The present article enquires into the possibility of using these provisions to safeguard the human creators in case AI transforms or creates a work. It contemplates that while the Copyright Act provides for a sufficient framework for the purpose, it lacks provisions regarding the role of humans in the creation, alteration by AI, misattribution, and proving the same. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Authorship, Moral Rights, Section 57, Copyright Act, 1957, Generative AI, Right of Integrity, Right of Attribution.

AI-enabled hazard detection is usually judged by whether it finds risky conditions. Prevention requires another step: somebody must have the time, authority and competence to respond. This article evaluates how that second step alters the interpretation of predictive safety performance. It reports a factorial computational experiment derived from a doctoral study of AI in occupational health and safety (OHS). Across 54 simulated operating conditions, five alert thresholds and 200 replications per condition, a score-based detector classifies 5,000 opportunities per replication. The design varies hazardous-opportunity prevalence (1%, 5% and 15%), score separation (1, 2 and 3), drift (0 and 0.75) and nominal response probability (0.40, 0.65 and 0.90), with response capacity limited to 500 alerts. At the reference threshold of 1.5, one 5%-prevalence, separation-2, no-drift condition yields mean residual hazardous opportunities of 180.8, 138.2 and 95.7 across the three response assumptions. With the same detector and nominal 65% response, imposing drift raises mean residual opportunities from 138.2 to 185.5. A sensitivity calculation also changes the preferred threshold when the relative weight of unresolved hazards and false alerts changes. The simulation shows why sensitivity, precision, workload and verified action belong in the same OHS decision model. All numerical data are computer-generated. The study does not report a deployed machine-learning system, workplace incidents, observed worker behaviour or injury reduction. Its contribution is a transparent stress test of the management choices that connect detection to prevention.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Smart contract vulnerabilities pose significant security risks to blockchain systems, potentially leading to severe financial losses. Existing methods face several limitations: (1) Program analysis-based approaches heavily rely on predefined patterns, lacking flexibility and adaptability to new vulnerability types; (2) Deep learning-based methods lack explanations for their detection results; (3) Large language model-based approaches suffer from high false positive rates. To address these challenges, we propose MOS, a smart contract vulnerability detection framework based on mixture-of-experts tuning (MOE-Tuning) of large language models. First, we conduct Continual Pre-training on a large-scale smart contract dataset to provide a domain-enhanced initialization for the subsequent MOE-Tuning process. Second, to provide reliable explanations for detected vulnerabilities, we construct a high-quality MOE-Tuning dataset through a multi-stage pipeline combining large language model generation and expert verification. Third, we design a vulnerability-aware routing mechanism that activates the most relevant expert networks by analyzing code features and their matching degree with experts, addressing the limitation of predefined patterns in program analysis approaches. Finally, we extend the feed-forward layers of the LLM after Continual Pre-training into multiple parallel expert networks, each specializing in specific vulnerability patterns. We also employ a dual-objective loss function: one for optimizing vulnerability detection and explanation performance, and another for balancing expert utilization through an auxiliary loss based on the scaled dot product of expert assignment frequencies and average routing probabilities, thereby improving model performance in complex vulnerability scenarios. Extensive experiments show that MOS consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in four foundational and historically significant vulnerability types (Reentrancy, Timestamp, Integer Overflow/Underflow, Delegatecall) with average improvements of 6.38% in F1 score and 4.84% in accuracy. The vulnerability explanations generated by MOS also demonstrate high quality, achieving positive ratings (scores of 3 and 4 on a 4-point scale) of 82.96%, 85.21% and 94.58% for correctness, completeness, and conciseness, respectively, through a combined approach of human evaluation and LLM evaluation. Extensibility experiments show that MOS effectively handles new vulnerability types (Access Control, Price Oracle Manipulation, Logic Errors, Lack of Input Validation, Slippage, and Risky First Deposit), consistently outperforming all baseline methods across six additional vulnerability categories. MOS achieved an average F1 score of 83.94% and an average accuracy of 87.82%, demonstrating its strong extensibility and flexibility in handling new vulnerabilities.

ABSTRACT Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-ToF MS) is now central to routine diagnostics, enabling accurate identification of microbial species. We assessed the performance of MSI-3, the updated release of the free online mass spectrometry identification (MSI) platform that now supports bacterial, in addition to fungal, identification. MSI-3 was benchmarked against MSI-2 and the Bruker MALDI Biotyper using two fungal data sets: (i) a reference panel of 669 sequenced isolates (Panel 1), and (ii) a real-world set of user-submitted spectra (Panel 2). MSI-3 and MSI-2 demonstrated equivalent performance across all fungal groups in Panel 1, with 97.8% (mean of 892/912) concordance at the species or species complex level, and a massive added value compared to the Bruker database for filamentous fungi (from about 41% to about 98%). MSI-3 exhibited slightly longer identification times than MSI-2 (1.52 vs 0.84 s per spectrum), but remained compatible with real-time online usage. The increased identification time is offset by a twofold expansion of the reference database and algorithmic improvements. In Panel 2, MSI-3 achieved comparable performance to Bruker for bacterial and yeast spectra, and outperformed Bruker for filamentous fungi, especially Aspergillus spp., Fusarium spp., and dermatophytes. A new “uninterpretable” category was introduced in MSI-3 to flag potential mixed or poor-quality spectra, facilitating result interpretation. Overall, MSI-3 marks a substantial advance in the MSI platform, uniting flexibility, broad taxonomic coverage, and artificial intelligence (AI) readiness. Its combined use with Bruker enhances diagnostic performance, positioning MSI-3 as a powerful and scalable standard for microbial identification in clinical and research settings. IMPORTANCE This article highlights the major importance of MSI-3 as a significant advancement in microbial identification using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-ToF MS). The expansion of the platform to bacterial identification, together with its already established fungal database and improved algorithms, now enables users to analyze mixed projects through a single workflow without additional sample handling or database switching. Used by more than 500 users worldwide, MSI-3 provides improved diagnostic performance, particularly for filamentous fungi, while offering a flexible and scalable solution for both clinical and research microbiology.

Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including ‘reservation’, ‘substitution’ and optional ‘insertion’ or ‘deletion’, before recommending mutations from protein language models, while surrogate evaluation and Pareto rewards shape policy training. We evaluate AbOptimizer on three therapeutic antibodies across multiproperty, data-limited and indel-inclusive optimization. In silico, AbOptimizer improves optimized properties and outperforms baseline methods. In vitro, selected variants show affinity-specificity co-optimization for emibetuzumab, improved affinity and specificity with largely maintained thermal stability for siltuximab, and indel-inclusive affinity optimization for trastuzumab. These results validate AbOptimizer as a practical framework for therapeutic antibody optimization. This study presents AbOptimizer, a computational framework that edits antibody sequences to improve multiple therapeutic properties. Tests on three antibodies show improved affinity, specificity and stability-related profiles.

Abstract Background Bronchoscopic biopsy in elderly patients with Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (AECOPD) presents high procedural risks. This case study analyzes the critical care nursing trajectory of an 76-year-old patient who survived a massive endobronchial hemorrhage and subsequent in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) during an interventional procedure. Resentation An 76-year-old male with severe COPD (FEV1 40% predicted) and hypertension underwent diagnostic bronchoscopy. Immediately following mucosal biopsy, the patient developed massive hemorrhage (approx. 300 mL), leading to acute asphyxia and pulseless electrical activity (PEA). The critical care nursing team initiated a rapid response, facilitating emergency tracheal intubation and localized hemostasis using epinephrine irrigation. Return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) was achieved after 6 min of advanced life support. Nursing interventions The nursing management focused on three critical phases: (1) Crisis Resource Management (CRM): utilizing rapid situational awareness to clear the airway and coordinate multidisciplinary resuscitation; (2) Post-ROSC Stabilization: implementing lung-protective ventilation and precise cuff pressure titration (25–30 cmH 2 O) to prevent re-bleeding and ventilator-associated complications; and (3) Secondary Prevention: managing the delicate balance between necessary anticoagulation for cardiovascular comorbidities and the risk of recurrent pulmonary hemorrhage during the recovery phase. Conclusion This case report documents the successful resuscitation of an 76-year-old male with severe AECOPD (FEV1 40% predicted) who developed massive endobronchial hemorrhage (~ 300 mL) and in-hospital cardiac arrest (pulseless electrical activity) during diagnostic bronchoscopy. Detailed preoperative risk stratification, intraoperative crisis resource management, and post-ROSC intensive care nursing interventions are described and analyzed. A comprehensive geriatric assessment, complete resuscitation parameters, functional outcomes, and a comparative discussion with existing literature on bronchoscopy-related airway hemorrhage are provided. A nine-phase nursing decision-making framework for high-risk bronchoscopy in elderly AECOPD patients is proposed. This report highlights the critical role of nursing-led situational awareness, structured crisis management, and dynamic hemodynamic titration in navigating catastrophic cardiopulmonary events in high-risk elderly populations. Clinical trial number not applicable.

The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into healthcare systems represents one of the most profound shifts in modern medicine, promising enhanced diagnostics, personalized treatments, and operational efficiencies. However, this transformation is not without its complexities, particularly in the realms of ethics and regulatory compliance. This narrative review synthesizes current literature, policy frameworks, and global case studies to examine the ethical challenges—such as algorithmic bias, data privacy, transparency, and equity—and the regulatory mechanisms designed to address them. Drawing from diverse sources including WHO guidelines, EU AI Act, FDA policies, and India’s National Strategy for AI, the article highlights the tension between innovation and safeguards. Key findings underscore the need for interdisciplinary collaboration to foster trustworthy AI, emphasizing human-centered design, inclusive data practices, and adaptive regulations. With the global AI healthcare market projected to exceed $500 billion by 2032, this review advocates for a balanced approach that prioritizes patient autonomy, societal equity, and sustainable development. Ultimately, ethical and regulatory frameworks must evolve in tandem with technology to ensure AI serves as a tool for healing rather than division.

documents.abstract: This review examines recent advances in neuromorphic computing for human-system interaction (HSI). Inspired by the nervous system, neuromorphic computing utilizes spiking neural network models, event-driven processing, and biomimetic hardware to enable ultra-low power computing. The review analyzes 35 scientific papers published up to May 2026, classifying applications into five categories: brain-computer interface and healthcare applications, human-robot collaboration, neuromorphic synapse and hardware, affective computing and emotion recognition, and neuromorphic sensors and human-machine interfaces. Compared to conventional computing techniques, neuromorphic computing exhibits low-power consumption and faster processing. Recent advancements in neuromorphic computers include the development of memristors, flexible synaptic devices, and self-powered sensory systems. However, challenges such as standardization of datasets, system scalability, hardware-software integration, system explainability, data security, and data privacy can be recognized as the future research topics of neuromorphic computing for HSI. Overall, neuromorphic computing provides a potential HSI solution for a safer, more intelligent, and more human-centered future.

Next Lab demonstrates that a student-led, studio-based innovation ecosystem can function as a leadership laboratory, where agency and ethical judgment develop through paid, real-stakes design work with external partners in emerging technologies. Grounded in heutagogy and agentic leadership, Next Lab at Arizona State University engages students in interdisciplinary, socially impactful design challenges that integrate artificial intelligence (AI), spatial computing, and game technologies. This chapter examines the lab’s studio-based model through institutional context, collaborative case studies, and evidence from alumni outcomes. Drawing on both qualitative reflections and survey data, the chapter shows how real-world, paid design work cultivates adaptive leadership, technical fluency, and ethical foresight. Together, these findings position the Next Lab model as a transferable framework for preparing graduates to navigate complex technological and societal futures.

Given the premise, supported by recent institutional, scientific and journalistic milestones, that Extraterrestrial Intelligences (ETIs) maintain a current and verifiable presence on Earth, this theoretical-hypothesis paper develops and defends the thesis that the question “what should be done?” admits no single, definitive or conclusive answer. Grounded in established epistemological traditions — situated knowledges, paradigmatic incommensurability and the underdetermination of theory by evidence — the paper argues that each observer’s answer depends on constitutive, experiential and contextual variables that differentially shape diagnosis, prognosis and attitude. The author’s biographical and investigative trajectory — four decades of ufological research documented in earlier peer-reviewed work and in two public pre-tragedy manifestos (2019 and 2022), including the paradigmatic case of Donato Cervantes and the Homeric Theater Hypothesis — centrally marked by the murder of his son by military police officers in November 2024, is explicitly positioned as a legitimate interpretive lens, not as an impossible neutrality. On this basis, ten scenarios for humanity’s destiny are analyzed with deliberately equivalent argumentative weight — inaction; open, massive contact; nuclear war; other human causes (resource depletion, global warming, genetically engineered virus); natural catastrophe; technical preparation for survival; replacement by artificial intelligence; inner transformation toward a “new human”; physical rescue by ETIs; and direct destruction by ETIs — each supported by multidisciplinary evidence (existential-risk literature, the twelve-criteria methodology for assessing contactee authenticity, hermeneutic analysis, and historical-geopolitical precedent). The paper concludes without breaking the tie among the ten alternatives, arguing that genuine uncertainty is intellectually more honest than a premature conclusion, and proposes, as a deliberately declared speculation, that ETIs themselves — if technologically advanced but not omnipotent — may share with humanity the same fundamental uncertainty about the future.

The study investigated occupational hazards associated with the teaching profession as perceived by secondary school teachers in Awka Education Zone of Anambra State. The study was guided by four research questions and four null hypotheses, which were tested at the 0.05 level of significance. A descriptive survey research design was adopted for the study. The study was conducted in Awka Education Zone. The zone has 65 public secondary schools with a total teacher population of 1,689. From this population, a sample of 304 teachers was selected using a simple random sampling technique. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire. Three education and measurement experts validated the instrument, and its reliability was established using Cronbach's alpha. The overall reliability index was 0.74. Mean and standard deviation were used to answer the research questions, while independent-samples t-tests were applied to test the null hypotheses. The findings revealed that respondents perceived physical, biological, psychosocial, and ergonomic hazards as associated with the teaching profession. Additionally, male and female teachers showed no significant differences in mean ratings across all four hazard categories. Based on the findings, it was concluded that occupational hazards are prevalent in the teaching profession in Awka Education Zone and that both male and female teachers are equally affected. The study recommended that, among other things, secondary schools train and deploy health and safety officers to monitor and mitigate biological hazards. Schools should establish and maintain hygienic practices, provide clean water and sanitation facilities, and ensure that teachers are adequately protected from communicable diseases through timely health education and medical check-ups.

documents.abstract: Background: Technological innovation is transforming endocrine surgery through new diagnostic and therapeutic tools that enhance precision, safety, and personalization of care. However, their clinical value depends on appropriate integration into evidence-based care pathways. This review summarizes the scientific discussions presented during the session “Innovations in Endocrine Surgery” at the 44th National Congress of the Italian Association of Hospital Surgeons, Palermo, Italy, 24–27 May 2026. Methods: A narrative review was conducted of presentations addressing ultrasound-guided thermal ablation, intraoperative neuromonitoring, lymphadenectomy in differentiated thyroid carcinoma, anaplastic thyroid carcinoma, intraoperative parathyroid identification, robotic and remote-access thyroid surgery, and laparoscopic versus robotic adrenalectomy. Session transcripts were analyzed according to the methodology described by Molteni et al. Findings were critically interpreted using current international guidelines and primary literature. Results: A consistent message emerged across all topics. Thermal ablation, near-infrared autofluorescence, neuromonitoring, and robotic platforms expand the technical possibilities of endocrine surgery by improving precision, safety, ergonomics, and, in selected patients, quality of life. However, their benefits consistently depended on three factors: appropriate patient selection, surgical expertise, and treatment within high-volume multidisciplinary centers. These principles were evident across thyroid, parathyroid, and adrenal surgery. Conclusions: Innovation in endocrine surgery derives its value not from technology itself, but from its appropriate application to individual patients. Although technological advances broaden surgical capabilities, clinical outcomes remain primarily determined by sound judgment, surgical expertise, and organization of care. Technology should therefore be regarded as an adjunct to, rather than a substitute for, high-quality clinical decision-making.

PURPOSE: To assess the accuracy of OpenEvidence relative to six leading large language models (LLMs) in answering refractive surgery multiple-choice questions, and to compare their performance with users of the American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) Basic and Clinical Science Course (BCSC) Self-Assessment Program. SETTING: Not applicable. DESIGN: Randomized questionnaire-based study using 225 questions from the refractive surgery section of the AAO BCSC Program. METHODS: OpenEvidence and 6 LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-5, Claude, Copilot, Gemini, and Grok) answered the same set of multiple-choice questions. Their accuracy was defined as the proportion of correct responses. Performance from 1,983 BCSC Self-Assessment Program users served as a benchmark. RESULTS: OpenEvidence achieved the lowest accuracy (76%) and performed significantly worse (P<0.05) than all six general-purpose LLMs. Claude achieved the highest accuracy (92%), followed by Grok (89.8%). ChatGPT-5, Copilot, and Gemini each scored an accuracy of 88%, and ChatGPT-4o achieved 86.2%. All models' lower 95% confidence interval bounds exceeded the 60% passing threshold. The average score of BCSC Self-Assessment Program users was 77%. All general-purpose LLMs scored significantly higher than BCSC Self-Assessment Program users (P<0.05), whereas OpenEvidence did not. CONCLUSIONS: OpenEvidence demonstrated significantly lower accuracy than the six evaluated general-purpose LLMs and did not exceed the BCSC Self-Assessment program user benchmark on this standardized refractive surgery multiple-choice assessment. This task-specific difference was not fully explained by response-format noncompliance and should not be interpreted as direct evidence of globally inferior medical knowledge or performance in open-ended clinical applications.

documents.abstract: This community service program concerned the preparation of AI-assisted teaching modules for teachers at SDN 07 Srengseng Sawah, South Jakarta. The partner assessment described constraints related to teachers’ time, understanding of teaching-module components, access to contextual examples, and limited experience in using AI for instructional planning. The main workshop took place on 3 October 2025. The activity report described preparation and coordination, delivery of materials, practical sessions using generative AI tools, direct assistance, and documentation. The reported outputs comprised teaching modules developed by teachers or teacher groups, a collection of prompts and templates, and guidance on reviewing AI-generated materials responsibly. Photographs in the report document the presentation session and direct assistance to teachers. Although the final report states that teachers’ digital literacy and AI-use skills increased, it does not present individual test scores, participant totals, or numerical pre- and post-test summaries. Accordingly, this article reports the implementation and outputs descriptively, without quantifying a learning gain. The experience illustrates the use of practical training and guidance to support teaching-module preparation while maintaining teachers’ role in validating instructional materials.

ABSTRACT Real‐time bidding (RTB) requires decisions in milliseconds under nonstationary market dynamics; traditional optimization and online RL suffer from sample efficiency, stability and generalization limitations. This study proposes a closed‐loop simulation framework coupling generative AI with deep reinforcement learning. A cascaded encoder combining a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) with a denoising diffusion probability model (DDPM) synthesizes high‐fidelity market states. A proximal policy optimization (PPO) agent trains in this environment via a three‐stage ‘generate, evaluate, optimize’ mechanism, with a dynamic feedback regulator forming a co‐evolutionary loop. Experiments on 47.82 million anonymized bidding records improve CTR by 23.7%, CVR by 31.2%, ROI by 23.5% over DQN and increase ROI by 6.1% over GAVE and 8.6% over DiffBid. A 2 × 2 factorial ablation confirms significant generator‐agent interaction ( = 0.37 ROI units, 95% CI [0.24, 0.51], = 0.008, = 0.024). Cross‐dataset transfer on iPinYou preserves rankings with 7.0% ROI advantage over GAVE; counterfactual OPE on real logs (SNIPS, doubly robust, auction replay) agrees with simulator ranking. The system achieves 87.4% sample utilization (distinct from GPU utilization 92.30%) and 14.8 ms mean inference latency (p50/p95/p99 = 12.4/18.7/23.1 ms; 100% SLA at 100,000 req/s). A live A/B test on a production platform is planned as future work.

Wireless mobile communication technology has gone through multiple generations of technical iteration, profoundly changing human communication modes and promoting social-economic development.Starting from digital 2G network, this paper sorts out the technical characteristics, core technologies and typical application scenarios of 2G, 3G, 4G and 5G mobile communication systems.It analyzes the evolution logic of mobile communication from voice-oriented service to mobile broadband and Internet-of-Everything.On this basis, the paper discusses the future developing trends of wireless communication technology, including 6G research, integrated sensing and communication, space-air-ground integrated network and artificial intelligence empowered network.Existing technical challenges are also summarized, which can provide reference for vocational teaching and related engineering research.

With the widespread use of technology in children's home learning, the home literacy environment (HLE) has been gradually digitalized, and the digital home literacy environment (DHLE) is put forward based on the HLE framework. However, the components and developmental dynamics of DHLE remain underexplored. Guided by the theory of planned behavior, this qualitative study investigated the components of the DHLE for English as a foreign language learners and how it is informed by parents’ perceptions. Data were collected from eight families through semi-structured interviews with both fathers and mothers of children aged 5–6 years, and hybrid thematic analysis was employed. Findings showed that the DHLE comprised digital and artificial intelligence (AI) devices and related resources, digital and AI-assisted language learning activities, and parental mediation strategies. Parents’ attitudes toward digital and AI-assisted learning, subjective norms including cultural values and societal influence, and perceived behavioral control, including parents’ time and resource constraints, digital and AI literacy, and English proficiency, jointly informed their intentions to support children's digital English learning, thereby influencing DHLE. The study extends the theoretical understanding of HLE by introducing a digital facet. It highlights the importance of parental mediation in children's language learning with digital technologies and contributes to the research on AI-supported education by exploring its application in home language learning environments, an area that has received limited attention. The study has implications for practice and policy in digital early childhood education.

Purpose To evaluate patient satisfaction and preferences for portable versus table-mounted visual field (VF) devices in a rural telemedicine setting and identify influencing factors. Methods We conducted a sequential explanatory mixed methods study at three Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) within the Alabama Screening and Intervention for Glaucoma and eye Health through Telemedicine (AL-SIGHT) study. Participants completed VF testing with table-mounted Humphrey Field Analyzer (HFA), tablet-based Melbourne Rapid Fields (MRF), and virtual reality (VR)-based VisuALL perimeters. Participants rated satisfaction, comfort, ease of use, and future testing preference. Chi-square tests assessed differences in device preferences. Twelve participants completed semi-structured interviews to explore reasons underlying preferences. Qualitative data were analyzed in NVivo 14 using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Among 271 respondents (mean age 60.4 years; 62.4% women), 50.6% preferred VR-based, 35.1% tablet-based, and 14.4% table-mounted for future testing (χ 2 (2) = 53.52, p < 0.001, Cramér’s V = 0.31). Satisfaction was highest for VR-based (56.9% very satisfied), followed by tablet-based (49.4%), and HFA (38.0%). VR-based perimeter was most frequently selected as the most comfortable (55.7%; χ 2 (2) = 63.33, p < 0.001, V = 0.34) and easiest to use (54.6%; χ 2 (2) = 71.96, p < 0.001, V = 0.36). Preferences did not vary significantly across demographic variables (all p > 0.05). Qualitative themes identified four key drivers: comfort and physical experience, visual experience, ease of use and interaction, and psychological and motivational factors. Portability and community suitability were valued. Conclusion Rural underserved patients strongly preferred portable visual field devices, particularly VR-based, over table-mounted HFA. Comfort, ergonomic flexibility, immersive visual experience, and simplicity of interaction were central determinants of preference. Portable perimetry may enhance patient-centered glaucoma monitoring within telemedicine programs and access in resource-limited settings.

General-purpose conversational artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used for health-related questions, including questions relevant to cancer care, although breast-cancer-specific prevalence and behavioural effects remain poorly characterised. Most evaluations ask whether an AI answer is accurate. That is necessary but incomplete. Clinically consequential effects may arise when a fluent, apparently personalised exchange changes a treatment preference, delays contact with the clinical team, reinforces reassurance-seeking, validates non-adherence, or converts population guidance into an individual-sounding instruction. We conceptualise this as a parallel pathway: an AI-mediated sequence of questions, answers and actions that is usually invisible to the treating team, absent from the medical record and unattached to professional responsibility, yet capable of re-entering formal care through its downstream consequences. We distinguish model error from pathway error and propose traceability, reversibility, and returnability to accountable care as safety properties beyond answer accuracy. Across four clinical domains, we propose distinct pathway failure modes: premature preference closure in surgical decision-making; escalation closure during treatment toxicity; repetitive reassurance-seeking and over-reliance in psycho-oncology; and loss of conditionality in perioperative recovery and lifestyle advice. These are hypothesis-generating mechanisms rather than empirically established dominant patterns. We propose a five-step clinical response - ASK, RECONSTRUCT, CLASSIFY, CHECK and RETURN - based on non-judgemental inquiry, proportionate documentation and explicit return-to-care boundaries. Regulation can govern products and deployed systems, but it cannot by itself reveal patient-initiated consumer AI use. Clinical services therefore need governance for the pathway as well as for the technology.

documents.abstract: Objective Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) lowers the threshold for producing work, not necessarily for learning. This study examines how an instructor kept an interdisciplinary AI course teachable for first-year art students, where that effort reached its limits, and how the instructor interpreted students' engagement with AI tools. Methods The study is a longitudinal practitioner self-study of a 12-week course taught in autumn 2025 at a higher vocational college in northwestern China. The data are the instructor's own reflective journals: structured entries written during the semester for Weeks 1–7 and retrospective accounts of Weeks 8–12 written after the semester ended. The two strata are reported separately. Reflexive thematic analysis produced 40 evidence anchors, five themes, one cross-cutting thread, and one central organizing theme, with a full audit trail. Results The instructor's repairs (translating content into everyday and discipline-specific tasks, working around broken or restricted lab equipment, and demonstrating on the teacher's computer) kept the course running. However, as content moved toward frontier tools that required paid accounts, computing resources, and prior AI experience, teaching drifted toward demonstration (“the more cutting-edge something is, the more it can only be demonstrated”). Across the semester the instructor recorded a recurring pattern, here termed a teacher-perceived low-threshold illusion , in which students appeared, in the instructor's account, to treat seeing, bookmarking, or one-click generation as equivalent to being able to do. The instructor associated this pattern with three co-occurring conditions: natural-language prompting and one-click generation, demonstration-only teaching, and a final assessment that students could complete without having attended. Participation could be high while, in the instructor's judgement, students gained little. Conclusion Pedagogical resilience reconstruction in AI teaching is bounded. Keeping an AI course running did not by itself make learning visible: the journals record a tension between engagement, product completion, and evidence of learning, not an established failure of learning. In-course repair reached limits shaped by access conditions and an inherited assessment format, and reconstruction of the course took place at the scale of the semester. We present pedagogical resilience reconstruction as an emerging construct for multi-case testing.

The BAPPEDA portal of Pariaman City previously served planning documents only as downloadable files, stored public complaints without processing, and offered no socioeconomic indicator data. During an internship at the Communication and Informatics Office of Pariaman City (1–31 July 2026), three artificial intelligence models were integrated into the portal through incremental development. First, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) question-answering model combines gemini-embedding-001 vectors, cosine similarity, a similarity threshold, and Gemini 2.5 Flash with schema-constrained JSON output. Second, a zero-shot Large Language Model (LLM) analyses each complaint in the background and recommends category fit, sentiment, and urgency without sending the complainant’s identity. Third, linear regression, ARIMA, and Prophet forecast the Human Development Index (HDI), poverty rate, open unemployment rate, and Gini ratio of Pariaman City; the best method per indicator is selected by backtesting, with linear regression as a fallback. An evaluation with 40 test questions moved the threshold from 0.65 to 0.74, which gave the highest balanced accuracy (62.9%) and raised out-of-scope rejection from 14.3% to 64.3%, while recall@5 fell from 92.3% to 61.5%. Backtesting showed that linear regression was most accurate for HDI (MAPE 0.44%), whereas ARIMA was best for the other three indicators (MAPE 3.80–8.19%). All 18 automated feature tests passed. The models turn the portal into an interactive service that supports information retrieval, complaint prioritisation, and development planning.
topics: Data Mining and Machine Learning Applications

documents.abstract: This study examined perceived influence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on computational skills and independent reasoning among pre-service teachers in College of Education, Akwanga, Nasarawa State. Five research questions and three hypotheses guided the study. Descriptive survey design was adopted. Population was 125 NCE mathematics pre-service teachers, sample was 100 (62 males, 38 females) selected by simple random sampling. Instrument was Artificial Intelligence on Computational Skills and Mathematical Reasoning among Pre-Service Teachers (AI-CSMRPT) with reliability of 0.82 Cronbach Alpha. Mean and SD answered research questions, one-way ANOVA and one-sample t-test tested hypotheses at 0.05. Findings revealed AI significantly influences computational skills (Grand M=3.09) by improving speed (M=3.24) and accuracy (M=3.18). Both male (M=3.18) and female (M=2.95) agreed, but significant gender difference existed (F=4.67 > 3.94). AI also influences independent reasoning (Grand M=2.90), with reliance on AI before attempting problems (M=3.16) highest. Both genders agreed (M=2.98 male, M=2.77 female) with significant difference (F=4.12 > 3.94). No significant difference between influence on computational skills (M=3.09) and independent reasoning (M=2.90), p=0.47. Study concluded AI enhances computation but creates alternative cognition that reduces independent effort if unguided. Responsible and ethical use of AI as supplement, gender-sensitive training, and institutional guidelines were recommended.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Background . The processing of medical data by artificial intelligence (AI) systems requires mandatory de-identification, yet simple removal of direct identifiers does not ensure anonymity. Modern AI models can re-identify individuals from indirect attributes, leaving a measurable residual risk. Objective . The aim of this study was to define the boundaries of de-identification in the AI era, systematize protection methods, and assess the actual attitudes of future physicians toward patient data handling. Methods . We conducted an anonymous cross-sectional survey of 1,283 medical university students and residents (me dian age 21 years). A self-administered questionnaire was used. Data were analyzed in Python (pandas) using chi-squared tests and Cramér’s V to compare differences across training levels. Results . Entering de-identified clinical text into cloud-based AI services was considered acceptable by 61.5 % of respon dents; 12.4 % had already uploaded real patient data, with 1.2 % doing so in identifiable form. Awareness of risks did not deter risky behavior: those who uploaded data had higher self-assessed risk knowledge (3.53 vs. 3.36, p < 0.0001), and 22 % admitted their actions were unacceptable yet continued them. The proportion of uploaders increased from 7.5 % in junior years to 21.0 % in senior years (χ² = 43.3, Cramér’s V = 0.18, p < 0.0001), while willingness to inform patients about AI use declined from 43.4 % to 24.4 %. Conclusions . Anonymity is not a state to be achieved but a continuous process of managing residual re-identification risk. Effective protection requires institutional bans on sharing de-identified data with public cloud services, adoption of methods with quantifiable residual risk (differential privacy, federated learning, homomorphic encryption), and strengthening education al curricula on ethics and information security.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Cybersecurity is changing from reactive, human-centered systems to highly autonomous cyber-capable agents (HACCAs) that can operate at machine speed and scale. This chapter introduces the Autonomous Fortress, an architectural framework that changes artificial intelligence from a tool that only supports analysis into a system that can make decisions, plan multiple steps, use different tools, and improve its actions through continuous reasoning. The core of the Autonomous Fortress is a large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent system (MAS). In this system, specialized agents for perception, correlation, analysis, and response work together as digital teammates to protect the environment. The framework combines different coordination methods, including a hierarchical supervisor model and swarm-based dynamic handoff, to support adaptive and context-aware decision-making. This approach goes beyond traditional machine learning systems that mainly depend on fixed rules and pattern matching. Although these secure-by-design mechanisms improve the defender’s ability to respond to cyber threats, high levels of autonomy also introduce new risks, such as prompt injection, memory poisoning, and cascading system failures. Based on national cybersecurity strategies and enterprise deployments from 2025 to 2026, this chapter presents both a technical and governance roadmap for building secure and resilient autonomous cyber defense systems in modern digital and cloud-native environments.

Pharmacogenomics (PGx) is an important component of precision medicine that uses genetic information to explain interindividual variability in medication response. Its clinical value is greatest when a validated genetic result can be translated into a specific therapeutic action, such as selection of an alternative drug, dose adjustment, intensified monitoring, or avoidance of a medicine associated with severe toxicity. The role of pharmacy practice is expanding because pharmacists possess expertise in pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, medication safety, medication therapy management, patient counseling, and longitudinal follow-up. This review examines the current role of pharmacogenomics in pharmacy practice, including clinically actionable gene–drug relationships, pharmacist-led testing, community and hospital implementation, electronic health record (EHR) integration, clinical decision support, medication safety, health equity, ethics, pharmacoeconomics, and future research. Evidence from pharmacogenomic implementation literature, Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium (CPIC) guidance, and regulatory resources was considered. Important examples include CYP2C19–clopidogrel, CYP2D6–opioids and selected antidepressants, DPYD–fluoropyrimidines, TPMT/NUDT15–thiopurines, HLA-B–abacavir, HLA-B–carbamazepine and allopurinol, SLCO1B1–statins, CYP3A5–tacrolimus, and VKORC1/CYP2C9/CYP4F2–warfarin. Pharmacists can contribute across the complete PGx pathway: identifying candidates, arranging testing, interpreting results, documenting genotype/phenotype, recommending evidence-based medication changes, communicating with prescribers, counseling patients, monitoring outcomes, and evaluating service quality. Contemporary implementation studies indicate that community-pharmacy delivery is feasible and generally acceptable, but barriers include pharmacist knowledge and confidence, reimbursement, workflow integration, interoperability, standardized guidance, privacy, and equitable access. A successful precision-pharmacy model should therefore combine pharmacogenomic information with clinical phenotype, comorbidities, organ function, concomitant medicines, patient preferences, and therapeutic monitoring. Future pharmacy research should emphasize prospective clinical outcomes, cost-effectiveness, implementation science, Indian population data, diverse genomic representation, and responsible artificial-intelligence-supported clinical decision support.

Abstract In recent years, Western philosophical inquiry has expanded beyond its traditional focus on humans, exploring questions about other‐ and more‐than human beings. This movement addresses a diverse array of topics, considering animals and elements of the natural world as well as growing attention to artificial intelligence. The Philosophy of Education Society (PES) and Educational Theory issued a joint call for paper proposals for the 2025 PES Pre‐Conference on the theme of “Philosophy of Education Beyond the Human.” This essay introduces the collection of articles developed through that call. The resulting special issue includes four articles that explore pedagogical relationships between humans and nonhuman or more‐than‐human entities (Hamilton, Krabbe, Lussier, and Pedersen), with two focused specifically on technology (Anderson and Khan). Together this set of articles offers insights into philosophy of education beyond the human that engage with a rich array of traditions of thought in philosophy and educational theory.

Abstract The inference of physical laws has traditionally relied on human intuition, analytical reasoning, and experimental observation. However, modern physics research is increasingly constrained by challenges such as high specialization, fragmented workflows, and limited computational resources, which impede scientific progress. To address these issues, we introduce PhysAgent , a novel multi-agent system powered by large language models (LLMs), designed to execute end-to-end scientific workflows—from hypothesis generation and computational modeling to data analysis and reporting. PhysAgent’s innovation lies in its specialized agent collaboration: a Mentor Agent guides scientific reasoning through Socratic questioning, a Student Agent handles technical execution (e.g., code implementation, DFT calculations), and a Leader Agent dynamically optimizes task scheduling and resource allocation. Integrating domain-specific tools like first-principles simulations (e.g., Quantum ESPRESSO, VASP), PhysAgent aims to improve reproducibility while maintaining human-in-the-loop refinement. We demonstrate PhysAgent as a proof-of-concept framework for recovering known physical relations from controlled data, including Kepler-law recovery from orbital trajectories and Newton-law recovery from force-motion data. Furthermore, it extends to ab initio materials modeling, automating electronic structure workflows (e.g., GaAs band-structure and density-of-states calculations). In addition, PhysAgent simulates complex real-world phenomena, such as raindrop flow on train windows. By harmonizing LLM-driven planning with domain-specific tools, PhysAgent provides a reproducible multi-agent workflow for physics data analysis and simulation. We provide a demonstration video of PhysAgent to illustrate its workflow and capabilities: https://b23.tv/emOilkC.

documents.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global threat to humankind, affecting food safety, health, and the economy. Moreover, it is evolving rapidly, resulting from the misuse and overuse of antibiotics in healthcare and agriculture a result which has emerged as a One Health challenge. It alters food systems by creating threats to food safety, food security, and public health. Such resistant microorganisms have the ability to persist and spread in the food systems, animals, water, and the environment. Such microorganisms are further sustained by the production of biofilms. There is increased demand for safe and sustainable alternatives as a result of the limited applicability of conventional antibiotics and chemical preservatives. Plant-mediated phyto-nanoparticles (PNPs) are emerging antimicrobials. A PRISMA-compliant literature search and bibliometric analysis were used to identify leading research trends and gaps. This review evaluates their applicability in different aspects of food safety and preservation and in mitigating AMR. It includes major foodborne pathogens, resistance mechanisms, biofilm formation, and synthesis of bioactive nanoparticles using plants. The main antimicrobial mechanisms of these nanoparticles include the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), disruption of the cell membrane, release of metal ions, enzyme inhibition, DNA damage, and interference with quorum sensing. This review includes their applicability in active food packaging, edible coatings, food preservation, and food processing surfaces. This review expands existing research by including the results of real food matrices and storage studies. The review incorporates the emerging applications of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in nanoparticles design, prediction of antimicrobial activities, and optimization of synthesis parameters, and trend identification. In general, PNPs have a lot of potential for sustainable approaches to food preservation. However, standardized methods, rigorous safety evaluation, AI/ML-assisted optimization, and real-food, in vivo , and industrial studies are needed for successful translation.
